runs.text: 1. How is the series generated using A, B, and N?
The series is generated using the formula:
First term = A + (2^0 × B)
Second term = A + (2^0 + 2^1) × B
Third term = A + (2^0 + 2^1 + 2^2) × B
The same pattern continues until N terms are generated.
For each query, the values of A, B, and N are given, and the corresponding N terms must be printed on one line separated by spaces.
2. What does Q represent in the series-generation problem?
Q represents the number of queries. Each query contains three values: A, B, and N.
For every query, the required series must be generated independently.
3. What do A, B, and N represent in the input?
A represents the starting value.
B is the value multiplied by the powers of 2.
N represents the number of terms to generate.
For example, if A = 5, B = 3, and N = 5, five terms must be generated.
4. What are the five basic rules of object orientation?
The five basic rules are:
The entire world is considered a collection of objects.
Every object has some purpose or usefulness.
Every object belongs to a particular category, type, or class.
Every object interacts with one or more other objects.
Every object has properties and exhibits behaviors.

6. What is a class?
A class is a blueprint used to define the structure and behavior of objects.
A class can contain:
Data members or attributes
Member functions or methods
Properties
Behaviors or functionalities
The class defines what an object will contain and what it can do.
7. What is an object?
An object is an instance or physical existence of a class.
A class defines the blueprint, while an object represents an actual instance created from that blueprint.
For example, Employee can be a class, while employee1 and employee2 can be objects of that class.

15. What are the four memory segments mentioned in the execution model?
The four segments mentioned are:

Heap segment

16. What happens when the JVM starts executing the

When the JVM starts execution, an activation record or stack frame is created for the
main(

The control then moves to the body of the

17. What is a stack frame or activation record?
A stack frame, also called an activation record, is the memory structure associated with a method while that method is executing.
When a method is called, its stack frame is created. When the method completes execution, its stack frame is removed.

23. What is garbage collection?
Garbage collection is the JVM mechanism that identifies objects in the heap that are no longer reachable through references and removes them to reclaim memory.
An object without any reference pointing to it is eligible for garbage collection.

runs.text: 26. When is memory allocated for an instance variable and a local variable?
Memory for an instance variable is allocated when its object is created in the heap.
Memory for a local variable is associated with the stack frame of the method in which the variable is declared and is created during method execution.
27. When is the memory of an instance variable and a local variable released?
The memory associated with an object becomes available for reclamation when the object becomes eligible for garbage collection.
A local variable's memory is released when the method's execution
completes
and its stack frame is removed.
28. Where
can instance
variables and local variables be accessed?
Instance variables can be accessed by methods belonging to the class, subject to access rules.
A local variable can be accessed only inside the method or block in which it is declared.
For example, a variable declared inside an if block cannot be accessed outside that block.
29. What are the default values assigned to instance variables?
Instance variables are automatically initialized with default values when an object is created.

31. What is an anonymous object?
An anonymous object is an object created without storing its reference in a reference variable.
For example:
The object is created, but no reference variable is used to hold it.
32. Why are anonymous objects used?
An anonymous object is used when an object is required only for a limited, typically one-time use.
For example:
The object is created and the method is called without storing the object reference.
33. What happens to an anonymous object after it is used?
Because no reference variable is retained for the object, it can become eligible for garbage collection after it is no longer reachable.
The same anonymous object cannot be reused through a reference variable because no reference to it was stored.
34. What are the four advanced pillars of object orientation?
The four advanced pillars are:
Encapsulation
Inheritance
Polymorphism
Abstraction
These are presented as the four major pillars supporting object-oriented programming.
35. What is the main advantage of encapsulation?
Encapsulation promotes data security by preventing direct access to important aspects of an object and providing controlled access instead.
36. How does inheritance help in software development?
Inheritance promotes code reusability.
When common properties and behaviors are already available in one class, another class can inherit them instead of rewriting the same code. This reduces development time.
37. How does polymorphism help in object-oriented programming?
Polymorphism allows one entity to take multiple forms.

The lecture connects this with code compactness and flexibility. Without multiple forms, more separate code may be required, increasing the amount of code and potentially increasing compilation and execution work.
38. What is abstraction?
Abstraction means hiding complex implementation details from the user and exposing the required functionality.
For example, when a user transfers money through an application, the user performs the transfer without needing to know the internal implementation that processes the transaction.
39. How do the four pillars contribute to an object-oriented application?
The lecture connects each pillar with a particular benefit:
Encapsulation → data security
Inheritance → code reusability and reduced development time
Polymorphism → flexibility and code compactness
Abstraction → hiding complex implementation from the user
Together, these concepts provide important characteristics for building object-oriented applications.
40. What is encapsulation as an object-oriented concept?
Encapsulation means giving controlled or indirect access to a very important aspect of an object rather than allowing direct access to it.
The important aspect is protected while the required functionality is made available through controlled access.
41. Why should direct access to an important aspect of an object be avoided?
An object may contain aspects that are critical to its proper functioning. Directly accessing or modifying such an aspect can damage the object or make it unusable.
The lecture uses examples such as the filament of a bulb and the motor of a fan to explain why important internal components are protected.
42. How does a bulb demonstrate the concept of encapsulation?
The filament is an important internal part of a bulb, but users do not directly access it.
Instead, a switch is provided as an indirect way to control the bulb. The internal filament remains protected while its required functionality is exposed through controlled access.
43. How does a fan demonstrate the concept of encapsulation?
The motor is an important internal part of a fan, but users do not directly access the motor.
Instead, controls such as a switch and regulator provide indirect access. The user can turn the fan on or adjust its speed without directly manipulating the motor.
44. How is encapsulation related to the idea of a capsule?
A medicine capsule contains the important medicine inside a protective covering. The medicine is not directly exposed; instead, it is accessed through the capsule.
Similarly, encapsulation protects an important aspect of an object and provides controlled or indirect access to it.
Therefore, encapsulation can be understood
as
giving indirect or controlled access to an important aspect of an object rather than exposing it directly.
